summary:
# Guía Lunar – Lunar Landing Site Exploration

Guía Lunar is a web-based lunar exploration and decision-support platform designed to help users investigate potential landing locations near the Moon’s south pole. As future lunar missions aim to explore this region, understanding terrain conditions, sunlight availability, and Earth visibility becomes increasingly important for mission planning.

The platform brings relevant lunar information together in an interactive, easy-to-understand dashboard. It focuses on three candidate locations: Shackleton Rim, De Gerlache Rim 2, and Malapert Massif. Using NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) terrain datasets, the project explores elevation and surface slope information to help users understand the physical characteristics of selected regions.

Guía Lunar also incorporates NASA/JPL Horizons API integration for investigating the changing positions and visibility of the Sun and Earth over time. This information is intended to support the exploration of illumination opportunities and communication-related conditions at different locations.

Built using React and Vite, the platform aims to make scientific data more accessible through a clear and user-friendly interface. It is a prototype that demonstrates how publicly available space data can be combined to support preliminary site comparison and exploration.
details:
Project Details – Guía Lunar

Project Name: Guía Lunar

Project Category: Space Exploration / Data Analysis

Project Type: Web-based Lunar Landing Site Exploration Platform

Problem Addressed:
Selecting potential lunar landing locations requires examining several factors, including surface elevation, slope, sunlight conditions, and Earth visibility. These factors are often presented through separate scientific datasets, making it difficult for users to explore and compare locations in one place.

Our Solution:
Guía Lunar is an interactive web platform that brings important lunar surface and environmental information together in a single dashboard. It focuses on three candidate locations near the lunar south pole: Shackleton Rim, De Gerlache Rim 2, and Malapert Massif.

Key Features:

  • Exploration of selected lunar south-pole locations.
  • Elevation and slope information using NASA LOLA terrain datasets.
  • Sun position and illumination analysis using NASA/JPL Horizons data.
  • Earth visibility investigation for communication-related planning.
  • A centralized dashboard for exploring and comparing candidate locations.

Technologies Used:

  • React.js
  • Vite
  • JavaScript
  • NASA LOLA datasets
  • NASA/JPL Horizons API
  • Vercel for deployment
